turnaround_reason: Years of heavy Homes.com/residential spend suppressed margins and dragged CSGP to a seven-year low near $26; Q2 FY26 marked the profitability inflection as Residential turned EBITDA-positive ($12M, first ever) and total adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to $184M.
bullish_points: Residential segment turned EBITDA-positive for the first time; the biggest cost drag is inflecting
Adjusted EBITDA more than doubled YoY to $184M; margins guided to expand from ~14.7% toward ~28% over next three quarters
FY26 adjusted EBITDA guide affirmed at $780-820M, above the initial February outlook
Fortress balance sheet (debt/equity ~14.5) funds the pivot without leverage risk
bearish_points: Management trimmed FY26 revenue guide ~$50M; growth is being sacrificed for profitability
Trailing PE ~176 -- still expensive on trailing earnings; thesis relies on forward margin expansion
Stock at seven-year low; sentiment and price momentum still weak (-27.7% vs 200d MA)
Commercial real estate backdrop remains soft
catalyst: Q3 FY26 showing sustained Residential EBITDA positivity and the guided margin ramp toward ~28%
suggested_trade: Starter spot position now (small-to-medium), add on confirmation of Q3 margin expansion
key_risk: Residential profitability proves lumpy/one-off and the margin ramp stalls, leaving a still-richly-valued stock without its inflection story
would_skip_if: Residential swings back to an EBITDA loss or FY26 EBITDA guide is cut
